node_intro.speaker: Abenthy
node_intro.text: Sit down, boy, and listen. The road is kind nine days in ten, but trouble keeps its own calendar. When it finds a troupe, you will have exactly four ways out. Do you know them?

choices.text: Run. Nothing worth having is worth dying for.
Stand and face it. We are Ruh. We do not run.

node_flee.speaker: Abenthy
node_flee.text: Right answer first, for once. Fleeing is not cowardice — it is choosing which ground your wagons cross. A good route beats a strong arm every time.

node_stand.speaker: Abenthy
node_stand.text: Brave, and foolish in equal measure. There are only two kinds of people who win fights they cannot avoid: the lucky and the dead. Learn the other doors first.

node_hide.speaker: Abenthy
node_hide.text: Second door: hide. Trouble is lazy — it looks where moving things catch the eye. Still hands, quiet feet, and the right beat of timing, and trouble forgets you were ever there.

node_talk.speaker: Abenthy
node_talk.text: Third door: talk. A reputation opens mouths before knives come out, and a friend who vouches for you is worth more than any blade. That is why troupes mind their standing in every town we play.

node_sympathy.speaker: Abenthy
node_sympathy.text: And the last door, saved for when the others are shut: sympathy. A working under pressure costs Alar and carries risk — slip the binding and it bites YOU, not him. But a boiled cup of ale has ended more brawls than swords ever drew.

node_practice.speaker: Abenthy
node_practice.text: Now practice. Down by the crossing there is a man spoiling for a fight with anyone in trouper's colors. Go on. Pick your door carefully — all four will open, but not all of them quietly.

text_by_flag.text: You handled the carter at the ford already? Then you know: every door works, if you pick it early enough.
